suggestions: Prefer fix-shape reasoning: detect replacement of raw length-based reads with safer string parsing helpers rather than guessing a specific memory bug label.
Inspect whether `readBytes` can return non-NUL-terminated data that is later consumed as a C string.
Trace the `parserrec->Password` data flow to string consumers and length assumptions instead of relying on the presence of a null/non-null check.
Compare contracts of `readBytes(f, length)` and `readString(f)` for termination, allocation size, and bounds handling.
Prefer consumer-side misuse analysis over superficial API-name matching; the vulnerability may arise when raw bytes are later treated as strings.
Avoid treating the `if (length != 0)` guard as proof of safety; it only gates emptiness, not string validity or bounds correctness.
